name: panos-mcp
description: Manage Palo Alto Networks Panorama and firewalls — config, commits, operations, logs, reports, objects, policies, updates, and certificates.
long_description: Provides AI assistants with structured access to the PAN-OS XML and REST APIs. Read and write candidate config with an explicit, separate commit step; run operational commands; pull logs and reports; manage address/service/tag objects and security/NAT policy rules over REST; drive content and software update lifecycle; and manage certificates. Works against Panorama (one credential set, with an optional per-call target serial routing to a managed firewall) or directly against a standalone firewall with the target omitted. Read-only validated against a PA-460 on PAN-OS 11.1.13-h6; mutating tools are unexercised against hardware.

panos_host.title: PAN-OS host
panos_host.description: Panorama or firewall hostname or IP (no scheme, no path). Required with no default: PAN-OS publishes no vendor base URL because the base URL is the appliance itself, not a shared API endpoint.

panos_api_key.title: PAN-OS API key
panos_api_key.description: API key sent in the X-PAN-KEY header, never in a URL. Leave blank only if panos_username and panos_password are set, in which case the server exposes panos_keygen to mint one; paste the minted key here afterwards. Until a key is set, only panos_status, panos_navigate, and panos_keygen are exposed.

panos_username.title: PAN-OS admin username
panos_username.description: Optional. Only used by the panos_keygen tool to mint an API key from credentials.

panos_password.title: PAN-OS admin password
panos_password.description: Optional. Paired with panos_username for panos_keygen.

panos_target.title: Default target serial
panos_target.description: Optional. Default managed-firewall serial number when talking through Panorama. Any tool call can override it with its own target argument.

panos_verify_tls.title: Verify TLS
panos_verify_tls.description: Optional. Defaults to true. Set to false ONLY for an appliance with a self-signed certificate; that disables certificate verification for this host, so the connection is no longer protected against interception. A PAN-OS appliance serving its factory certificate (subject == issuer) needs it.

panos_rest_version.title: REST API version
panos_rest_version.description: Optional. REST API version path segment. Defaults to v11.1.
